build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player character moves in a top-down view and fires a gun that shoots projectiles toward the cursor, with enemies firing dense bullet patterns that must be dodged. Score 0 if there is no shooting or bullet patterns.
A dodge-roll ability grants brief invincibility frames, allowing the player to pass through bullets. The roll has a visible animation and short cooldown. Score 0 if no dodge mechanic exists.

Rooms are connected in a roguelike structure: clearing enemies opens exits, and the player chooses which room to enter next. Death restarts the run from floor 1. Score 0 if there is no room structure or roguelike progression.
Gun pickups found between rooms offer weapon swaps with distinct firing patterns (shotgun spread, railgun pierce, bouncing orbs, rapid fire). Score 0 if only one weapon exists throughout.

The player has limited health (hearts or HP) that depletes when hit by bullets, with visible damage feedback and a game-over state when health reaches zero. Score 0 if the player is invincible or has no health system.
At least 3 floors with 5-7 rooms each, with different room themes, enemy compositions, and increasing difficulty per floor. Score 0 if only one floor exists.
At least 5 distinct gun types with different projectile behaviors, fire rates, and tactical uses. Score 0 if only one gun exists.
At least 4 distinct enemy types per floor with different bullet patterns (radial, aimed, spiral, random burst) and movement behaviors. Score 0 if only one enemy type exists.
Each floor ends with a boss that has at least 3 distinct attack phases with escalating bullet pattern complexity. Score 0 if no floor bosses exist.
A run-end screen shows rooms cleared, enemies defeated, guns found, and floor reached, with a victory screen for completing all floors. Score 0 if the game ends abruptly with no summary.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, a Start Run control, and gothic or dungeon-themed imagery. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to room combat to room transitions to boss encounters to floor interstitials without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.
The HUD clearly shows health, current gun, room map or progress indicator, and floor number in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine game state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: dodge-roll shows motion blur or ghost, hits on enemies flash, bullet patterns are clearly visible against backgrounds, and room clears trigger a celebration effect. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, rooms, enemies, bullets, guns, HUD, and interstitials with a consistent gothic-dungeon palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
The player character, enemies, bosses, bullets, guns, and room tiles use real sprite art with distinct designs and readable silhouettes. Score 0 if primary gameplay elements are unstyled rectangles.
Animation brings rooms to life: dodge-roll animation, bullet pattern motion, enemy attack windups, boss phase transitions, and explosion effects. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with gothic frames, custom fonts, or dungeon-styled elements rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
